note: Sixth straight quiet week for admin moves - no hires, exits, or board personnel actions turned up dated within the past 7 days across any of the fifteen districts and trusts. The real news was Tuesday's Nov. 3 referendum election: Tri-Creek's and Union Township's operating referendums passed, Michigan City's was rejected. Valparaiso's superintendent search (McCall departed over the summer) and East Porter's and LaPorte's recent leadership changes remain out of the 7-day window.

stories.headline: Tri-Creek operating referendum passes
stories.body: Voters approved Tri-Creek's eight-year operating referendum in Tuesday's general election, capped at $0.1738 per $100 of assessed value and about $3 million a year, earmarked for bus transportation, student programs, and school safety.

stories.headline: Union Township referendum leading big in early returns
stories.body: Union Township's operating referendum - up to $0.35 per $100 of assessed value, about $3.37 million a year - was passing roughly 64% to 36% in Porter County's unofficial Nov. 3 returns; final certification wasn't yet confirmed.

stories.headline: Michigan City operating referendum rejected by voters
stories.body: Michigan City Area Schools' proposed eight-year operating referendum - capped at $0.2998 per $100 of assessed value and $10 million a year - was voted down in Tuesday's general election.
